claim: Chloroidium sp. UTEX 3007 was isolated from multiple locations in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
source: To investigate the phenomic and genomic traits that allow green algae to survive in deserts, we characterized a ubiquitous species, Chloroidium sp. UTEX 3007, which we isolated from multiple locations in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract and supported by Figure 1a-b showing isolation locations

claim: Chloroidium sp. UTEX 3007 accumulates a broad range of carbon sources, including several desiccation tolerance-promoting sugars.
source: Metabolomic analyses of Chloroidium sp. UTEX 3007 indicated that the alga accumulates a broad range of carbon sources, including several desiccation tolerance-promoting sugars and unusually large stores of palmitate.
evidence: Supported by metabolomic data presented in the manuscript

claim: Chloroidium sp. UTEX 3007 accumulates unusually large stores of palmitate.

claim: Chloroidium sp. UTEX 3007 can grow in salinities from zero to 60 g/L.

evidence: Supported by growth assay data presented in the manuscript

claim: Chloroidium sp. UTEX 3007 can grow heterotrophically on more than 40 distinct carbon sources.
